summary: Turtles and rushers are in crisis: turtles quit at 83% (mostly boredom after long draws), rushers quit at 67% (frustration after getting crushed in R2). Round 2 is the choke point—overall win rate drops to 45% and quit rate spikes to 19%. A physics bug (!stuck during BLOCK) appears in 3 turtle logs and likely inflates turtle boredom. Cheesers exploit a sweep-heavy strategy to win fast (avg 42.5s) with low damage taken (meanHpLoss 66.6). (Verification: 0 of 21 claims did not match the recomputed value; 1 cited seeds did not exist in the runs and were removed.)

findings.title: Turtle archetype mass-quits from boredom after drawn-out Round 1
findings.narrative: 15 of 18 turtles (83%) quit, nearly all after Round 1 or 2 with reason 'boredom'. Their Round 1 avg duration is 78.7s (vs 43.9s overall) and 10/18 Round 1s end in draws. Three turtles also hit a !stuck@… BLOCK invariant violation, which likely freezes the round and amplifies boredom.
findings.suggestion: Add a sudden-death timer (e.g., 60s) or damage-over-time after 45s to force resolution; fix the BLOCK stuck invariant.

findings.suggestion: Fix the BLOCK state machine so it cannot enter a stuck state; add watchdog to auto-resolve stuck rounds.

findings.title: Speedrunner frustration quit spike in Round 3 (29%) despite high skill
findings.narrative: Speedrunners win 60% overall and play fast (27.1s avg), but 4 of 9 (44%) quit—two specifically after Round 3 from 'frustration' (p0135, p0136). They likely hit a skill ceiling where R3 rival reads their optimized patterns. Small N (9 players) so treat as signal, not proof.
findings.suggestion: Add R3 variant that breaks memoized patterns (randomized rival style) to reward adaptation over memorization.
